To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the notion of hypothetical knowledge is equivalent to the notion of knowledge about counterfactuals; 2) hypothetical knowledge cannot be modeled in the framework of epistemic logic, but can be captured in the framework of conditional logic; and 3) the axioms that are needed to model hypothetical knowledge are unreasonable in general.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the notion of hypothetical knowledge, which was introduced to capture a type of counterf actual reasoning that is necessary for the solution of a game of perfect informa tion, is in fact not necessary for this purpose.
